meta.sourcePrompt: MASTER ERP HARDENING + FULL PROJECT REMEDIATION PROMPT v1.0.0

meta.note: Phase 0 is discovery only — no code changed to produce this plan. Findings are grounded in direct code inspection, not the master prompt's assumed defect list.

p0.title: pgQuery('BEGIN') is not a real transaction
p0.evidence: pgQuery() calls pool.query() which acquires+releases a connection per call; BEGIN and the following statements are not guaranteed to run on the same connection under concurrency.
p0.correctPatternExample: src/lib/masterdata/masterDataData.ts, src/lib/import/importData.ts, src/lib/numbering/service.ts (pool.connect() -> client.query('BEGIN') -> ... -> COMMIT -> release())
p0.recommendedFix: Extract withTransaction(fn) helper in src/lib/db/index.ts using pool.connect(); migrate the two broken call sites; add a rollback regression test.

p0.title: No centralized bilingual error catalog
p0.evidence: src/lib/errors/ does not exist; apiError() maps exceptions to an English-only message + HTTP status with no code/fa/en/severity/module shape.
p0.recommendedFix: Build src/lib/errors/ (catalog, factory, formatter, codes) per Phase 7 of the master prompt; wire into apiError() without breaking existing callers.

p1.note: 5 real empty catches, all localStorage/video best-effort, none touch money/inventory/audit. Not P0.

phaseQueue.title: Approval engine RULE-004 fail-safe: missing matrix rule must never silently auto-approve
phaseQueue.evidence: REAL P0 found by direct code audit (not assumed): src/lib/erp/approvalData.ts createApprovalRequest had `const autoApproved = plan.length === 0` which conflated "no matrix rule matched this docType/amount" (a config gap) with "a matched rule explicitly has zero levels" (a real business decision) -- exploitable live because approval_matrix rows are admin-editable (upsertMatrixRule/deleteMatrixRule) so narrowing/deleting a range silently starts auto-approving that range. Fixed: resolveApprovalPlanExplicit() in matrix.ts returns {plan, ruleMatched} distinguishing the two cases; createApprovalRequest now auto-approves ONLY when ruleMatched=true and the matched rule has zero levels; when NO rule matched at all it falls back to a mandatory single administrator-role approval level (fail-safe, never silent-approve) and raises an idempotent business_alert (kind=approval_matrix_gap) naming the exact doc type/amount/request so the gap is visible and fixable from /admin/approvals. 3 new unit tests + live-PostgreSQL proof: deleted all payment_request matrix rows, submitted a real 500,000,000 payment via the real treasury API -> stayed status=pending with a 1-level administrator plan (never silently approved) + the config-gap alert was written with the exact detail; restored one rule and confirmed a normal payment still routes to finance_manager as designed (no regression). tsc/lint/vitest(1300)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: Inventory RULE-012/013: negative-stock guard + atomic transfer on the manual moves route
phaseQueue.evidence: REAL P0 pair found by direct code audit: /api/admin/erp/inventory/moves POST wrote a transfer as TWO separate non-transactional pgQuery inserts (half-transfer risk if the second insert failed after the first committed) AND had ZERO available-quantity check before writing a negative issue/transfer-out inv_moves row (unlike the guarded 26.19 shipment-issue path via canHold) -- a manual Issue or Transfer could drive stock negative with no check at all. Fixed: canIssueDirect(onHand, qty) pure guard added to stockOps.ts (default BLOCK, this repo has no negative-inventory policy setting to reuse); the route now wraps both the transfer (both legs) and any outbound single-row move in withTransaction (Phase 1a helper), serialized per product×warehouse via pg_advisory_xact_lock to close the concurrent-request race, computing on-hand from inv_moves inside the same transaction/lock before writing. 4 new unit tests + live-PostgreSQL proof: received 10 units, over-issue of 11 correctly blocked HTTP 400 with zero rows written, exact issue of 10 succeeded; received 5 more, over-transfer of 6 blocked, exact transfer of 5 succeeded with BOTH legs atomically written sharing one ref (WH1 to 0, WH2 to 5). tsc/lint/vitest(1301)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: GL posting atomicity (RULE-001/RULE-006): header+lines+source-link commit as one transaction
phaseQueue.evidence: REAL P0 found by direct code audit: the shared GL entry-insert core (glPosting.ts insertPostedEntry) plus the two highest-volume real posting paths (salesData.postSalesInvoiceToGl -- every confirmed sales invoice -- and purchasingData.postPurchaseInvoiceToGl) all inserted the journal header, then LOOP-inserted lines, then updated the source-document gl_entry_id link, using bare pgQuery with NO transaction. A failure on any line insert (or the link update) left a POSTED, UNBALANCED journal entry on the books, or a posted entry the source document did not know about (breaking the gl_entry_id idempotency guard on retry -- risking a double post). Fixed: insertPostedEntry now takes an injected TxQuery; postSalesPaymentToGl/postCustomerRefundToGl/postPurchasePaymentToGl/reverseEntry (glPosting.ts) and postSalesInvoiceToGl/postPurchaseInvoiceToGl (sales/purchasingData.ts) each wrap their ENTIRE header+lines+link sequence in one withTransaction call (Phase 1a helper) -- commits together or none of it lands. Verified: zero regressions across the full committed regression suite (22 suites, live PostgreSQL) including every GL-specific assertion (26.23 invoice auto-post+idempotency, 26.24b BUG-008 AP non-negative, 26.26b BUG-020 reversal/closed-period, trial-balance-still-balanced); PLUS a direct forced-mid-transaction-failure test against real Postgres proved a header insert + one line insert (before the forced throw) rolled back completely -- zero leaked rows -- the exact posted-unbalanced-entry defect class this closes. tsc/lint/vitest(1301)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: GL posting atomicity sweep: revaluation, intercompany, budget lines
phaseQueue.evidence: Continued the Phase 1c sweep (same defect class) into the remaining candidates found by grepping for files with 2+ INSERT statements and no withTransaction: erp/revaluationData.ts bookRevaluation (FX revaluation GL post -- header+loop-lines, same unbalanced-entry risk), erp/ledgerData.ts bookIntercompany (WORSE: posts TWO full journal entries across two companies in a bare loop -- a mid-loop failure could post company As entry and silently drop company Bs, breaking the intercompany balance across two separate companies books), and erp/budgetData.ts replaceLines (DELETE-then-loop-INSERT with no transaction -- a failure mid-loop silently lost budget lines, old ones deleted, new ones only partially written). All three now wrap their full sequence in withTransaction. Verified: zero regressions across all 22 committed regression suites on real PostgreSQL; bookIntercompany directly exercised live against real Postgres (2 companies, 2 posted entries, 2 balanced lines each, correctly stamped to each companys company_id) -- the identical withTransaction mechanism was already directly rollback-proven with a forced mid-transaction failure in Phase 1c. tsc/lint/vitest(1301)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: BACKLOG (not yet fixed): draft-creation atomicity gaps found during phase7b
phaseQueue.evidence: Both gaps fixed with the same withTransaction pattern: finance/journal/route.ts POST (create) and the update op each now wrap header+lines(+template) as one transaction; erp/sales/documents/route.ts POST (create-or-update) wraps header write + DELETE-old-lines + loop-insert-new-lines as one transaction. Verified: zero regressions across all 22 committed regression suites on real PostgreSQL; direct live proof -- created a real invoice with 2 lines (confirmed 2 rows), then updated it with 3 different lines through the real HTTP update path (confirmed exactly 3 new rows, old 2 fully replaced, no orphans). tsc/lint/vitest(1304)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: Double-submit guard (RULE-025 / 26.32-class): wire runOnce into sales-document and journal-entry create
phaseQueue.evidence: REAL gap found: the 26.32 double-submit fix (runOnce) was NEVER applied to any ERP module -- only its original 3 targets (skills/timeline/crm-leads). Two genuinely concurrent identical POSTs could create two duplicate invoices or two duplicate journal entries. Fixed: wired runOnce into erp/sales/documents POST (create branch only -- update targets a specific row, naturally idempotent) and erp/finance/journal POST (always a create). SECOND real bug caught by the live-concurrency test itself: nextNumber() was called BEFORE runOnce/withTransaction, so even though only one row was actually written, every concurrent request still minted its own document/entry number (numbering-sequence gaps) and -- worse -- reported ITS OWN locally-minted number back to the caller instead of the one really stored on the row (4 of 5 concurrent callers were told a WRONG entryNo for the one real entry). Fixed by moving nextNumber() inside the runOnce-guarded transaction closure. Verified live against real PostgreSQL: fired 5 genuinely concurrent identical invoice-create POSTs -> all 5 responses returned the same id, exactly 1 row in sales_documents; fired 5 genuinely concurrent identical journal-entry-create POSTs -> before the numbering fix, all 5 shared the same id but reported 5 DIFFERENT entryNo values (only 1 matched the DB); after the fix, all 5 responses report the identical, correct entryNo matching the single stored row. tsc/lint/vitest(1304)/build/9 audits all clean.

phaseQueue.title: Approval Engine deep audit: transactional atomicity, concurrency, and repo-wide SoD gap
phaseQueue.evidence: Deep audit of the whole approval engine (lib/approval/{matrix,engine,escalation,analytics}.ts, lib/erp/approvalData.ts, api/admin/erp/approvals). Confirmed already-correct: fail-safe missing-rule handling (earlier phase2), pure derived state machine (approvalState recomputes status from an append-only actions log — REJECTED/APPROVED/CANCELLED->anything else is structurally impossible since actOnRequest refuses any further action once status leaves pending/changes_requested), escalation never grants approval (only changes notification target), RBAC/IDOR (unauthorized approver rejected by resolveActor, never trusts client-supplied approverId). THREE real defects found and fixed: (1) actOnRequest (the actual decide path) was NOT transactional -- read row, INSERT action, re-read, UPDATE request status, conditionally touch a linked HR request, all bare pgQuery -- a mid-sequence failure could leave an orphan action with no matching status update; (2) NOT concurrency-safe -- two decisions racing on the same request had no serialization, a lost-update/duplicate-action race; (3) THE BIG ONE: separation-of-duty (isSeparationViolation) was a hardcoded 2-item allowlist (journal_entry, payroll_period) -- 16 of 18 registered approval-matrix doc types (payment_request, purchase_order, asset_disposal, budget_change, ...) had ZERO maker-checker enforcement; a user could create AND approve their own payment/purchase, confirmed live. Fixed (1)+(2) by wrapping the whole decide sequence in withTransaction with a pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the request id plus a duplicate-decision idempotency guard; fixed (3) by defaulting SoD to every registered doc type (was: allowlist, now: opt-out-only design matching the approval-matrix RULE-004 fail-safe philosophy). A first version of fix (3) used matrix.ts DOC_TYPES alone and silently dropped payroll_period protection (a real, separately-used doc string outside the matrix engine) -- caught by the FULL regression suite (28.3-الف/ب payroll SoD assertions failed) before this was pushed, fixed by explicitly re-adding payroll_period, verified 22/22 green again. 5 new unit tests for isSeparationViolation (zero existed before, despite it being a security control) + live PostgreSQL verification of all of: A valid approval succeeds, B missing rule blocks, C unauthorized approver blocked, D maker cannot self-approve (the fixed bug, confirmed both before-fix-fails and after-fix-blocks), E three genuinely concurrent identical decisions on one request -> exactly 1 fulfilled + 2 rejected + exactly 1 approval_actions row + correct final status, F a forced mid-transaction failure -> zero leaked rows, request untouched. tsc/lint/vitest(1309)/build/9-audits/22-regression-suites all clean.

phaseQueue.title: Sales / Order-to-Cash deep audit: credit-limit + overpayment concurrency races
phaseQueue.evidence: Deep audit of the sales domain (sales.ts/salesData.ts/glPosting.ts, sales/{customers,documents,payments} API routes). Honest classification of the order-to-cash chain: quotation/sales_order/invoice/AR/payment/GL/returns are genuinely IMPLEMENTED (pricing, credit control, invoice, AR, payment allocation, GL auto-posting, return/refund via BUG-013). Inventory Reservation and Delivery are NOT_IMPLEMENTED as part of the sales flow -- confirmed by direct code inspection (zero references to inv_moves/inv_reservations/stock checks anywhere in sales.ts/salesData.ts/the sales documents route); the Inventory module (26.19) is a fully separate subsystem never wired to sales_documents. Discount-approval routing (discount_approval doc type) is registered in the approval matrix engine but never actually triggered from the sales flow -- also NOT_IMPLEMENTED as an active control (document immutability after confirm is the only real discount-tampering guard, and it is solid). TWO real, confirmed, exploitable TOCTOU concurrency defects found and fixed: (1) the credit-limit guard on invoice confirm read the live AR balance then wrote status=confirmed as two separate unlocked statements -- two genuinely concurrent confirms for the SAME customer, each individually within the limit but together exceeding it, could both pass; (2) the overpayment guard on payment recording had the identical pattern -- two concurrent payments against the same invoice could both read the same alreadyPaid sum and both insert, together exceeding the invoice total. Both fixed with pg_advisory_xact_lock-serialized withTransaction wrapping the whole check+write sequence (same pattern used throughout this remediation). Live-PostgreSQL verified: (A) a complete cash sale end-to-end (customer->invoice with 10% discount + 9% VAT, confirm+auto-GL-post, full payment) -- pricing math exact, GL entries reconciled to the penny (Dr AR 9,810,000 / Cr Revenue 9,000,000 / Cr VAT 810,000, then Dr Bank/Cr AR 9,810,000 on payment, net AR = 0, subledger total == GL total); (B) the credit-limit race: two invoices each individually within a 10,000,000 limit, confirmed concurrently -- exactly 1 succeeded, 1 correctly blocked with the bilingual ERP-SALES-CREDIT-LIMIT-EXCEEDED error, confirmed by direct DB inspection; (C) the overpayment race: two concurrent 6,000,000 payments against a 9,000,000 invoice -- exactly 1 succeeded, 1 correctly blocked, total paid stayed at 6,000,000; (D) the full return/refund lifecycle on a paid invoice -- confirmed the BUG-013 design works exactly as documented (a business_alert is raised naming the unsettled credit, AR is shown honestly negative rather than silently hidden, matching the projects own stated financial-integrity rule); (E) API authorization -- unauthenticated requests correctly 401, malformed ids correctly 400-validated, nonexistent document id correctly rejected (400 Not found -- logged as a P3 status-code-convention finding, not fixed: this exact badRequest(Not found) pattern is a pre-existing, widespread, non-security convention across dozens of routes repo-wide, out of scope for a sales-domain-focused fix). Zero regressions: full unit suite (1309/1309), lint, build, 9 governance audits, and all 22 committed regression suites all green.

phaseQueue.title: Sales final verification: duplicate-audit-event fix, transaction rollback, customer-not-found 500
phaseQueue.evidence: Re-ran duplicate-invoice concurrency against the CURRENT build (not relying on a prior phase result): 5 concurrent identical invoice-create requests -> exactly 1 row, but found a REAL bug: audit_logs got 5 success rows for the 1 real creation, because logAction ran unconditionally after runOnce regardless of whether that specific call was the original write or a replayed duplicate. Same bug found WORSE in finance/journal create-and-post: a replayed duplicate also re-ran makerCheckerGate (creating a SECOND approval request per duplicate) and postEntryById (which correctly no-op'd but then made the route return a spurious 400 to what should have been a successful response). Fixed both with a didWrite flag set only inside the closure that actually executes (never set for a runOnce-short-circuited replay) gating logAction/post/approval side effects. Verified live: 5 concurrent invoice creates -> 1 row, 1 audit row (was 5); 5 concurrent create-and-post journal requests -> 1 entry, 1 audit row (was would-be 5), 0 duplicate approval requests. Forced-mid-transaction-rollback re-verified on a real payment-recording-shaped sequence (payment INSERT + document status UPDATE, forced failure before commit) -> zero orphan payment, zero status change, zero GL entries, zero audit rows -- ALL OR NOTHING confirmed with fresh evidence. Repo-wide inventory/COGS search re-confirmed fresh (not reused from Phase 3): zero linkage in either direction between sales and inventory code -- reservation/delivery/stock_movement/COGS all NOT_IMPLEMENTED as part of the sales flow. Full financial reconciliation with a fresh, odd-amount invoice (percentage discount+tax producing fractional Rial values) -- every layer matched exactly to the cent: subledger outstanding == GL net AR, revenue/tax subledger == GL revenue/tax postings, payment == GL bank debit == GL AR credit, and every entry balanced (debit==credit). A THIRD real defect found while testing the error catalog: a nonexistent customerId on invoice create fell through to a raw PG foreign-key-violation (23503, not special-cased by apiError) and surfaced as an unhandled HTTP 500 -- exactly the master prompt's own ERP-SALES-CUSTOMER-NOT-FOUND example. Fixed with a new catalog code + explicit existence check, verified live -> real HTTP 404 with the correct bilingual message. 1 new unit test (8 total in errors.test.ts). Zero regressions: unit 1310/1310, lint, build, 9 governance audits, all 22 regression suites all green.

phaseQueue.title: Procurement/Purchase-to-Pay: payment overpayment guard, doc.save atomicity+idempotency, receiveDocument concurrency, approval maker/checker+locking
phaseQueue.evidence: Read the actual procurement implementation (purchasingData.ts + route.ts) before assuming anything. Confirmed procurement has its OWN separate approval mechanism (purchase_approvals + decideApproval), distinct from the shared lib/approval/* engine used by finance/sales -- did NOT migrate it onto the shared engine (out of scope, would be a new architectural feature); hardened it in place instead. Found 3 real, confirmed defects: (1) recordPayment had ZERO overpayment/status guard at all (worse than the sales bug, which at least had a racy guard) -- fixed by reusing sales.ts's pure validatePayment (no duplicated validation logic) inside a withTransaction + pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the document id; (2) saveDocument's header-write + delete-lines + insert-lines sequence ran as bare unlocked pgQuery calls with no transaction -- fixed with withTransaction, matching the identical fix already applied to sales/documents and finance/journal; route.ts's doc.save case also had no double-submit guard on create -- added runOnce with a didWrite-gated audit log (no duplicate success rows on a deduped replay); (3) receiveDocument (the GRN receiving flow, which DOES write real inv_moves rows -- confirmed procurement has real inventory integration, unlike sales) read-then-updated received_qty with no transaction/lock, allowing two concurrent receipts on the same line to both read the same remaining qty and over-receive -- fixed with withTransaction + advisory lock keyed on the document id. Also hardened decideApproval: added a maker/checker guard (a document's creator cannot approve/reject their own request), a duplicate-decision guard (same approver+level rejected), and wrapped the whole insert-decide-advance sequence in withTransaction + advisory lock. LIVE VERIFICATION on a real running build + real PostgreSQL (not just unit tests): (a) 5 concurrent identical doc.save PR creates -> exactly 1 purchase_documents row, exactly 1 audit_logs row; (b) 2 concurrent receive requests each asking for 70 of a 100-qty line -> received_qty settles to exactly 100 (never 140), confirmed via inv_moves SUM and purchase_document_lines.received_qty; (c) 2 concurrent 7,000,000 payments against a 10,000,000 confirmed invoice -> exactly one succeeds, the other is rejected with the overpayment error, purchase_payments SUM stays exactly 7,000,000 (never 14,000,000); (d) maker/checker live-verified: the same user who created and submitted a PR is rejected with 'The creator of this document cannot approve or reject it' on doc.approve; (e) forced-transaction-rollback on receiveDocument (invalid warehouse id mid-sequence) -> threw, zero inv_moves rows written, received_qty unchanged, document status unchanged -- ALL OR NOTHING confirmed. Full regression suite re-run against a fresh live PostgreSQL DB: found 2 suites broken by the new, stronger guards (sim-2621.ts's single-admin approval flow tripped the new maker/checker rule; verify-2624b.ts's BUG-008 proof assumed paying a draft invoice would succeed-then-be-corrected, which the new overpayment/status guard now blocks outright) -- fixed sim-2621.ts by minting a second seeded approver user distinct from the document creator, and rewrote verify-2624b.ts's assertions to match the new (strictly stronger) contract, logged as CC-007 in docs/governance/contract-changes.md per rule 5. Re-ran: ALL regression suites -- 22 total, green. Full quality gate: tsc 0 errors, ESLint 0 warnings, vitest 1310/1310 passed, build clean, all 9 governance audits clean (tokens/content/deps/links/i18n/ui/tenancy/theme/nav/shell/rbac all 0 budget-violations). Honestly NOT verified/NOT implemented and NOT claimed otherwise: three-way match (PO+GR+Invoice qty/price/tax tolerance) -- no evidence found of this check anywhere in the procurement code, reported as not_implemented, not fabricated or silently built. Duplicate-decision guard on decideApproval verified by code reading + the same transaction/lock pattern proven live elsewhere in this phase (recordPayment, receiveDocument, doc.save), but not independently re-run as its own concurrent-HTTP scenario due to the single-seeded-admin-user constraint of the verification environment (would require a second live login session).

phaseQueue.title: Three-Way Match (PO/Receipt/Invoice) engine + payment gate, real matching/rules; duplicate-invoice/moadian/notification honestly reported as absent business concepts, not fabricated
phaseQueue.evidence: DISCOVERY FIRST (per the phase's own mandate): read purchase_documents/purchase_document_lines schema before writing any code. Confirmed zero matching logic existed anywhere in the repo (grep for three_way/matching/tolerance found nothing procurement-related). Confirmed a supplier invoice is just a purchase_documents row with doc_type='invoice' -- there is NO 'supplier invoice number' field anywhere in the schema (doc_no is the SYSTEM-generated Numbering-Engine number, not the vendor's own invoice number), so 'duplicate supplier invoice number' is not a bug to fix -- it is a business concept the product has never modeled, reported honestly as not_implemented/missing product policy rather than inventing a uniqueness constraint on a field that doesn't exist. Confirmed convertDocument already copies lines 1:1 in sort_order across order->receipt->invoice -- the smallest architecture consistent with this model is line-level ancestry (po_line_id/receipt_line_id, self-referencing FKs, nullable) rather than a new framework. Confirmed Moadian (سامانه مودیان) only ever wires to SALES documents (grep of moadianData.ts) -- this is not a gap to close, it reflects Iranian tax law correctly (the SELLER files مودیان e-invoices, not the buyer), reported as an architectural fact in remaining_work, not mislabeled as a missing feature. IMPLEMENTED: pure engine src/lib/erp/threeWayMatch.ts (matchLine/overallMatchStatus, no I/O, 15 unit tests covering every Phase-3/4/5 quantity/price/tax scenario from the master prompt verbatim -- PO100/Receipt100/Invoice100->matched, PO100/Receipt80/Invoice100->mismatch, PO100/Receipt100/Invoice120-> mismatch, PO100/Receipt80/Invoice80->matched). Exact price/tax comparison only (EPS=0.005 for float rounding) -- explicitly did NOT invent a tolerance percentage, since no tolerance mechanism exists anywhere else in the codebase; documented as a real, separate, undecided business rule in remaining_work instead of guessing a number. Schema: po_line_id/receipt_line_id/match_status on purchase_document_lines, match_status/match_checked_at/match_override/match_override_reason/match_override_by on purchase_documents, all idempotent ALTERs; erp_settings key 'three_way_match_mode' (off/warn/block, default 'warn') -- the EXACT precedent already used by 26.25's credit_guard_mode, reused rather than inventing a new pattern. convertDocument populates the lineage during order->receipt and receipt->invoice conversion. matchPurchaseInvoice(invoiceId) reads the lineage and runs the pure engine; recordPayment re-runs the match FRESH inside its existing locked transaction (never trusting a stale persisted value) before inserting a payment -- 'pending' (no PO/receipt behind a standalone invoice, the normal case for ad-hoc invoices this system has always supported) never blocks; only a genuine 'mismatch' is gated, and only in block mode, and only absent an administrator override (overrideMatch: reason required, audited, role-gated -- no silent bypass). New error catalog code ERP-PURCHASING-PAYMENT-BLOCKED-MISMATCH (bilingual, reuses the existing catalog infrastructure, not a second one). Two new route actions (doc.match, doc.matchOverride) under the SAME existing erp.purchasing RBAC permission -- no new approval engine, no new error catalog. LIVE VERIFICATION on a real running build + real PostgreSQL: built a full PO->Receipt->Invoice chain via real HTTP calls and confirmed exact lineage (invoice line's poLineId/receiptLineId correctly point at the PO and receipt lines) and a 'matched' result; tampered an invoice's qty/price directly in the DB to force 'mismatch' and confirmed doc.match detects it; confirmed default 'warn' mode allows payment on a mismatched invoice while persisting match_status and raising a business_alert (verified row in business_alerts); switched to 'block' mode and confirmed a mismatched invoice's payment is REFUSED with the bilingual ERP-PURCHASING-PAYMENT-BLOCKED-MISMATCH error and zero purchase_payments rows written; confirmed an administrator override unblocks the SAME invoice for payment and is itself recorded (match_override/reason/by columns populated); confirmed 5 concurrent identical supplier-invoice-create HTTP requests deduplicate to exactly 1 row via the EXISTING Phase-4 runOnce guard (generic across every doc_type, so it already covers invoice creation with no new code); forced a mid-transaction failure inside recordPayment (bad vendor_id FK) AFTER the three-way-match gate had already run its read+persist -- confirmed zero orphan payment row, unchanged paid_total/status, AND the match_status write itself rolled back with everything else (all-or-nothing, including the NEW code path); ran a full untampered PO->Receipt->Invoice->confirm->pay cycle and reconciled real PostgreSQL values end to end: AP credited by exactly the invoice total, AP settles back to the exact pre-transaction baseline after payment, inv_moves quantity/value match the receipt exactly, trial balance debit=credit to the cent. phaseQueue.title: Sales -> Inventory -> Fulfillment -> COGS -> GL: reservation core hardening, sales-order reservation integration, delivery, idempotent COGS posting
phaseQueue.evidence: Discovery FIRST (docs/engineering/phase6-inventory-sales-audit.md): confirmed sales_documents/sales_document_lines had ZERO structural link to inv_moves/inv_reservations/inv_shipments (grep + direct code reading) -- Sales and Inventory were fully disconnected modules, exactly as the phase assumed. Per the phase's own explicit instruction not to duplicate concepts, reused this existing engine rather than building a second one. SCHEMA (minimal, additive): sales_documents.warehouse_id (nullable FK -- sales orders had NO warehouse concept at all; a genuine, necessary, minimal product decision, documented); inv_shipments.sales_document_id + gl_entry_id (nullable FKs, link fulfillment back to the order it fulfills + idempotent COGS posting guard). FIXED (real, confirmed defects): (1) createHold -- now runs its read-check-insert inside one transaction + pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed per product x warehouse (`stock:{productId}:{warehouseId}`), closing the exact 'Stock=10, A wants 7, B wants 7' race the phase's own spec describes; onHandOf/holdsOf/inTransitOf/stockStateFor gained an optional injected TxQuery param (default pgQuery, so every existing standalone caller -- the inventory-ops route, sim-2621.ts -- is unaffected) so the lock scope composes correctly into a caller's larger transaction. (2) createShipment -- the pre-loop validate-then-separate-insert-loop pattern (itself racy) is now one transaction; createHold is called with the SAME injected query so its own lock joins the same atomic scope. (3) advanceShipment -- the whole transition (status re-check, hold consumption, inv_moves writes, serial updates, header update) now runs inside one transaction serialized per shipment id (`shipment:{id}`), closing a real double-issue race on two concurrent 'ship' calls for the same shipment. Also found and fixed a genuinely necessary, pre-existing, adjacent bug: the sales-document `convert` operation's INSERT...SELECT never copied `product_id` when converting quote->order or order->invoice, which would have made the new Sales->Inventory link impossible for any order that started as a quote (the normal path) -- fixed (copies product_id + carries forward warehouse_id) and wrapped in a transaction (it had none). BUILT (new, real, live-verified): src/lib/erp/salesFulfillment.ts -- reserveSalesOrderTx (reserves every product line of a confirmed order against its warehouse, wired into the sales/documents route's EXISTING confirm branch for doc_type='order', mirroring the invoice credit-check's exact transaction+lock precedent; insufficient stock on ANY line rolls back the whole confirm, no partial reservation; idempotent -- guarded by status!=='confirmed' so a repeat confirm never double-reserves); releaseSalesOrderReservation (cancel/void before delivery releases reservations, never a physical stock mutation, since nothing was ever issued); deliverSalesOrder (ONE self-contained transaction, locked per order id, that shrinks the order-level reservation -- consume + re-create the remainder, matching this codebase's append-only-ledger idiom rather than mutating a qty in place -- writes real inv_moves issue rows, and posts idempotent COGS (Dr 5000/Cr mapped-inventory-account) all atomically; delivery_qty > reserved_remaining is rejected using the LIVE reservation row itself as the ledger, never a denormalized counter that could drift). New route action PUT .../sales/documents {op:'deliver'}, gated by a new RBAC sensitive op erp.sales:deliver (added to SENSITIVE_OPS, audit:rbac re-verified clean at 40 ops). Two new bilingual error-catalog codes actually wired to behavior: ERP-SALES-INSUFFICIENT-STOCK (reservation gate), ERP-SALES-DELIVERY-EXCEEDS-RESERVATION (delivery gate). Audit events on every new mutation: inventory.reservation.created, inventory.reservation.released, delivery.confirmed, cogs.posted. LIVE POSTGRESQL VERIFICATION (scripts/verify-phase6-sales-inventory.ts, committed, 23 assertions, wired into ci-regressions.ts): reservation invariants (onHand/reserved/available); a REAL two-concurrent-transaction race (Stock=10, two 7-unit holds fired via Promise.allSettled against the same live PG connection pool) -- exactly one succeeded, reserved settled to 7 and available to 3, never 14/-4; a forced mid-transaction failure (FK violation on the second of two inserts) -- zero partial reservation rows survived; 5 concurrent DISTINCT holds against ample stock all succeeded (no lost writes under lock contention); the full order-confirm-reserve, partial-deliver (3 of 4), over-deliver-rejected (5 > 1 remaining), final-deliver-the-remainder chain, with COGS reconciled to the cent (4 units x 15,000 cost = exactly 60,000 Dr COGS / Cr Inventory); a REAL two-concurrent-delivery race against a shared 10-unit reservation (two 7-unit delivery attempts) -- exactly one succeeded, total delivered settled to 7, never 14; cancel-before-reservation (0 rows released, honestly a no-op) vs cancel-after-reservation (exactly 1 row released); a final trial-balance tie-out across everything posted in the run. ALSO verified over real HTTP against a running production build + live PostgreSQL: created a sales order with warehouseId via the actual POST route, confirmed it via the actual PUT route (reservation row appeared for real, ref=SO-{orderId}-{lineId}), attempted an over-delivery (got the exact bilingual ERP-SALES-DELIVERY-EXCEEDS-RESERVATION response, both languages, HTTP 400), then delivered correctly (shipment + idempotent COGS entry created, full audit trail present in audit_logs), then confirmed unauthenticated access (401) and a nonexistent order id (400, not a raw 500) both correctly rejected. phaseQueue.title: Finance/AR/AP/GL/Tax hardening: closed 6 confirmed duplicate-GL-posting concurrency defects (reverseEntry double-reversal, 4x invoice/payment-GL double-post races, postEntryById idempotency)

Fixed all 6, each locked per source id via pg_advisory_xact_lock, matching this codebase's own established pattern (the exact fix already applied in Phase 4/5/6 to purchasing/inventory functions): (1) reverseEntry (P0) -- concurrent void/reverse could double-reverse an entry's financial effect while only one reversal stayed linked; (2) postSalesInvoiceToGl (P0) -- concurrent invoice confirm/re-post could double-post revenue/AR/VAT; (3) postPurchaseInvoiceToGl (P0) -- same class on AP; (4) postSalesPaymentToGl/postCustomerRefundToGl (P1) -- concurrent payment/refund GL posting could double-post cash movement; (5) postPurchasePaymentToGl (P1) -- same class on AP; (6) postEntryById (P2) -- the manual journal-post action was a bare read-then-write; now locked and IDEMPOTENT (returns {ok:true,alreadyPosted:true} on a repeat rather than an error), matching the master prompt's own explicit requirement that a retry after a successful POST report the same logical success -- logged as CC-008 in docs/governance/contract-changes.md, with the pre-existing regression test updated to match the new, intentionally-idempotent contract. LIVE POSTGRESQL VERIFICATION (scripts/verify-phase7-finance.ts, committed, 21 assertions, wired into ci-regressions.ts): 5 genuinely concurrent postSalesInvoiceToGl calls on the SAME invoice -> exactly one journal entry (was capable of producing 5 before the fix); same live proof for postPurchaseInvoiceToGl (AP side), postSalesPaymentToGl, and reverseEntry (5 concurrent void attempts on the same posted entry -> exactly ONE reversal, original stays posted and correctly linked -- the real double-reversal race, closed); a forced mid-transaction failure (FK violation) during a hand-rolled GL insert inside the SAME lock scope the real posting functions use -> zero orphan journal entries survived, the source invoice was never linked to a partial entry; a full AR lifecycle (invoice->GL->payment->GL) reconciled against real DB values (subledger AR = invoice total - payment total, matched exactly); tax reconciliation against the real configured 9% VAT rate, GL Taxes Payable credited by exactly the sum of the run's invoice VAT; a final trial balance across the whole run tied out exactly (debit == credit); 5 concurrent postEntryById calls on the same draft journal entry all succeeded idempotently with exactly one posted row (no duplicate status flips, no error on the concurrent duplicates). Full regression history re-run: found and fixed a real regression in the PRE-EXISTING verify-2623.ts suite caused by the postEntryById contract change (its old assertion expected an error on a repeat post; the new, intentionally-idempotent behavior returns success) -- updated the test to assert the new contract and logged CC-008 per governance rule 5, rather than silently weakening either the fix or the test. Re-ran: ALL 25 regression suites green (24 prior unchanged + this phase's new suite). Full quality gate: tsc 0 errors, ESLint 0 warnings, vitest 1328/1328 passed (unchanged -- no new pure unit-testable logic was introduced this phase, only transactional/locking hardening of existing SQL sequences), build clean, all 9 governance audits clean (no new sensitive ops, no new error-catalog codes, no RBAC/tenancy changes were needed -- this phase hardened internal concurrency safety, it did not add new user-facing surface area). phaseQueue.title: Treasury/cash-bank/returns/refund hardening: closed 8 confirmed duplicate-financial-mutation concurrency defects across a previously un-audited second payment path (Treasury payment_orders/receipt_transactions) plus sales/purchase return and refund races
phaseQueue.evidence: Discovery first (docs/engineering/phase8-treasury-audit.md): mapped the real Treasury/cash/bank architecture before changing anything. Made one major architectural discovery: this repository has TWO distinct, both-real payment-recording surfaces — the Phase-4/7-hardened sales_payments/purchase_payments direct path, AND a genuinely separate Treasury module (payment_orders/receipt_transactions, Phase 26.14) with its own maker/checker lifecycle and its own GL posting — that had NEVER been audited for concurrency/atomicity in any prior phase. Found 8 confirmed defects, all the same root-cause class (read-then-write races / missing transactions) already fixed elsewhere in this codebase but present here for the first time: (1) Treasury createPayment (P0) — zero idempotency guard, 5 concurrent identical requests could create 5 payment_orders rows. Fixed: runOnce. (2) Treasury processPayment (P0) — bare unlocked read-status/UPDATE/post-GL/UPDATE sequence, no transaction; concurrent process calls could double-post GL, a mid-sequence crash could orphan a posted entry. Fixed: one transaction locked per payment id, now idempotent (alreadyProcessed). (3) Treasury createReceipt (P0) — the whole allocate-across-invoices/mark-paid/insert-sales_payments/post-GL/insert-receipt sequence was unlocked and non-transactional; concurrent receipts for the same customer could double-allocate. Fixed: one transaction locked per customer id. (4) Cross-module (P0) — createReceipt inserted a REAL sales_payments row but never stamped its gl_entry_id, so Phase 7's postSalesPaymentToGl (gated on gl_entry_id IS NULL) could later post a SECOND, genuinely duplicate GL entry for money Treasury already booked. Fixed: the sales_payments row is now stamped with the same gl_entry_id the Treasury receipt posts — proven live: calling postSalesPaymentToGl on a Treasury-created payment now correctly returns alreadyPosted:true. (5) Treasury's local postGl helper (P1) — minted a non-sequential ad-hoc entry number and never called assertPostable, meaning a Treasury payment/receipt could post into a CLOSED/LOCKED fiscal period while the direct path already correctly rejects that. Fixed by reusing the shared insertPostedEntry/accountIdByCode primitives (which already enforce this) instead of a local reimplementation — closing this gap as a direct consequence, verified live: a payment dated into a closed period is rejected and the whole transaction (including the earlier 'processing' status write) rolls back to 'approved', not left stuck. (6) createSalesReturn (P0) — the entire read-invoice/read-lines/compute-amount/read-priorReturned/validate/insert sequence was unlocked; two concurrent 'return 7' requests on a 10-unit invoice could both read priorReturned=0 and both succeed, a real over-return. Fixed: one transaction locked per invoice id. (7) purchasingData convertDocument's return path (P0) — the 'already returned' pre-check and the actual return-document insert were two separate, unlocked operations; purchase returns copy the FULL invoice (all-or-nothing), so a double-return here means crediting 200%. Fixed: saveDocument gained an optional externalQuery parameter (the same pattern already used for createHold/createShipment in Phase 6); the return path now locks per source invoice and shares one transaction with the check and the insert. (8) settleReturnIfPaid (P0) — the 'a refund already exists for this credit note' idempotency check was a bare SELECT separate from the INSERT; concurrent settlement calls could double-refund. Fixed: refund-mode branch now runs inside one transaction locked per credit note id (the credit-mode branch was already idempotent via its fingerprint-keyed upsert, left unchanged). LIVE POSTGRESQL VERIFICATION (scripts/verify-phase8-finance.ts, committed, 24 assertions, wired into ci-regressions.ts): 5 concurrent identical Treasury payment creates -> exactly 1 row; 5 concurrent process calls on the same approved payment -> exactly 1 GL entry; a payment dated into a closed fiscal period is rejected with the whole transaction (including the status write) rolled back; a Treasury receipt's sales_payments row is proven to carry the same gl_entry_id the receipt posts, and calling the direct-path poster on it afterward is proven to correctly no-op instead of double-posting; 5 concurrent DISTINCT receipts for the same customer total exactly the sum of their amounts (no lost/duplicated writes); a real 2-concurrent-transaction sales-return race (10-unit invoice, two 7-unit returns) settles to exactly 700,000 returned, never 1,400,000; a real 2-concurrent-transaction purchase-return race (full-invoice return) settles to exactly the invoice total, never double; 5 concurrent refund-settlement calls on the same credit note resolve to exactly 1 refund payment row; a forced FK-violation failure mid-transaction (after a real header insert) inside the same lock scope createSalesReturn uses leaves zero orphan credit notes; final trial balance across the whole run ties out exactly. Full regression history re-run: 26/26 suites green (25 prior unchanged + this phase's new suite) — no contract changes were needed this phase (every fix is additive concurrency/atomicity hardening with no externally-observable behavior change to a passing case). Full quality gate: tsc 0 errors, ESLint 0 warnings, vitest 1328/1328 passed (unchanged — this phase's fixes are transactional/locking hardening of existing SQL sequences, no new pure-testable logic), build clean, all 9 governance audits clean (no new sensitive ops, error-catalog codes, RBAC changes, or schema migrations were needed — every fix reused an existing gl_entry_id-style guard column or an existing shared posting primitive).

phaseQueue.evidence: Discovery first (docs/engineering/phase9-financial-control-audit.md): answered all 7 of the phase's own explicit questions about Treasury supplier-payment <-> AP semantics directly from the code before touching anything. phaseQueue.title: Closed the Treasury supplier-payment overpayment gap with unapplied-cash recording (no schema migration); found and fixed a genuine same-vendor concurrent-allocation P0 race
phaseQueue.evidence: Discovery answered the phase's 15 explicit questions directly from the code before writing anything: purchase_payments.document_id was already a nullable column (no schema change needed) and vendorPosition's AP balance query already sums purchase_payments.amount by vendor_id with NO document_id filter, so an unapplied-cash row is automatically included in the vendor's balance with zero additional code. Grepping the codebase for the symmetric customer-side concept (receipt_transactions.advance) showed it has been write/display-only with no consumption path since Phase 8 -- decisive evidence used to deliberately NOT build future-invoice consumption of the supplier-side unapplied balance this phase (parity with the existing customer-side limitation, not an oversight; documented explicitly rather than left silently undone). Confirmed via canTransitionPayment's FLOW map that no Treasury payment reversal mechanism exists at all, on either side -- a genuine, pre-existing, out-of-scope gap, documented honestly rather than built as unplanned scope creep. Implementation: processPayment (src/lib/treasury/paymentData.ts) now persists any amount allocateReceipt could not place against an open invoice as its own purchase_payments row (document_id=NULL, same vendor_id, same gl_entry_id, a descriptive note) inside the exact transaction/lock Phase 8-10 already established -- one commit covers the allocation loop, the unapplied row, and the GL post. Reuses allocateReceipt's existing {allocations, advance} split unchanged -- zero duplicated allocation logic, zero new tables/columns. processPayment's return type gained unappliedAmount (additive, backward compatible with every existing caller). A genuine P0 concurrency defect was discovered writing the mandatory two-DISTINCT-payments-same-vendor-same-invoice race test (Promise.all, not sequential): the pre-existing treasury_payment_process:${id} advisory lock only serializes repeat calls on the SAME payment id, not two DIFFERENT payments racing to allocate against the SAME vendor's open invoices -- reproduced live as an actual overpay (paid_total driven to 1,400,000 against a 1,000,000 invoice). Fixed with a second advisory lock, treasury_ap_allocate:vendor:${vendorId}, serializing the whole read-decide-write allocation sequence per vendor; re-run 3x consecutively with zero failures after the fix. A second, smaller defect was found and fixed in the same pass: party_ref is free text, not a real FK, so a stale/unresolvable vendor id (exercised by Phase 9's own committed regression script) could reach an INSERT and violate purchase_payments_vendor_id_fkey; processPayment now confirms the vendor actually exists before attempting any allocation or unapplied-cash recording, falling back to the pre-existing GL-only behavior otherwise. Live-PostgreSQL verified (scripts/verify-phase11-financial-controls.ts, 37 assertions, committed regression suite): single-invoice overpayment split exactly into allocated+unapplied with money conservation proven numerically; exact-payment case creates zero unapplied rows; multi-invoice partial+unapplied split; idempotent re-processing of an already-completed payment returns a stable unappliedAmount and creates no duplicate row; 5 concurrent identical process calls on the same payment resolve to exactly one GL entry and one unapplied row; 2 concurrent DISTINCT payments racing the same invoice settle to exactly 1,000,000 allocated + 400,000 unapplied, never overpaid, proven both standalone and inside the full 29-suite regression run; two independent forced-rollback scenarios (mid-transaction failure, and closed-fiscal-period rejection) each leave zero partial state including zero orphan unapplied rows; a fresh trial balance ties out after every scenario. Full regression history: 29/29 suites green (28 prior + this phase's new suite), re-run twice, plus 3 additional standalone re-runs of the new suite alone to confirm the concurrency fix is deterministic, not lucky timing. tsc/eslint/vitest(1328)/build/12 governance audits all clean -- no new error codes, RBAC ops, or schema migrations needed. Honest boundaries carried forward: future-invoice consumption of unapplied supplier cash and Treasury payment reversal (of any kind) remain explicitly not_implemented, both justified and documented rather than silently skipped.

phaseQueue.title: Closed the Phase 11 future-invoice-consumption gap: unapplied supplier cash now automatically settles a vendor's newly-opened invoices, with no schema migration and no new GL event
phaseQueue.evidence: Discovery answered the phase's 15 explicit questions directly from the code before writing anything: purchase_payments.document_id was already nullable (Phase 11), vendorPosition's AP balance query already sums purchase_payments.amount by vendor_id with no document_id filter (so consumption's net-zero row pair needs zero balance-formula changes), and no CHECK constraint on purchase_payments.amount forbids a negative value -- confirmed the existing schema is sufficient without a migration. Grepped receipt_transactions to confirm the customer-side advance concept remains write-only (unchanged since Phase 8), and traced postPurchasePaymentToGl to find the one real landmine: it treats gl_entry_id IS NULL as an unposted real cash payment and will post a brand-new Dr AP/Cr Bank entry for it -- so consumption's two new rows per allocation step (a negative source-side adjustment + a positive invoice-side allocation) both had to be stamped with the SOURCE row's own already-posted gl_entry_id, never NULL, to stay correctly inert to that poster (Section 8 Option A: no new GL event, verified live). Implementation: consumeUnappliedForVendor (src/lib/treasury/paymentData.ts) derives each unapplied source row's remaining balance from the append-only ledger itself (own amount + Sum of linked negative adjustment rows, never a mutated counter -- the same discipline the GL reversal convention already enforces) and reuses allocateReceipt unchanged as the per-source distribution primitive, oldest-source-first x oldest-invoice-first -- zero duplicated allocation logic. Locks the SAME treasury_ap_allocate:vendor:${vendorId} advisory key Phase 11's processPayment already takes before its own AP allocation, deliberately the same lock domain rather than a new one, so a new Treasury payment being processed and a consumption run for the same vendor can never interleave. Wired automatically into confirmPurchaseInvoice (purchasingData.ts) right after its GL post -- deliberately placed OUTSIDE the existing GL-post try/catch, since a consumption failure must never trigger the GL-post-failure status-revert on an invoice whose GL entry already committed (a structural bug that would otherwise leave a posted GL entry behind a reverted document status) -- found and fixed during implementation, before any test ran. Live-PostgreSQL verified (scripts/verify-phase12-financial-controls.ts, 51 assertions, committed regression suite): one-to-one, one-unapplied-to-many-invoices, and many-unapplied-to-one-invoice consumption; an unapplied balance larger than the target invoice correctly leaves the remainder unconsumed; idempotent re-consumption after full settlement is a stable no-op with zero new rows; two concurrent consumption calls against the same unapplied balance and against the same invoice each settle to exactly the available amount, never double; a consumption run racing a genuinely distinct new Treasury payment for the same vendor (Promise.all) never over-allocates and conserves money exactly; explicit consumption against an invoice inside a fiscal period closed AFTER the invoice was opened still succeeds (no new GL event, so the period gate correctly does not apply, by design not by omission); confirming an invoice posts exactly one new GL entry -- consumption itself adds zero, and calling postPurchasePaymentToGl on every consumption row correctly refuses to post (alreadyPosted=true), proving no phantom Dr AP/Cr Bank entry is ever created; a forced mid-transaction rollback leaves zero orphan rows, the invoice and the original unapplied balance both exactly restored; an 8-case precision matrix (0.01 through 1,000,000.01) shows zero drift in both the invoice's paid_total and the remaining unapplied balance; a fresh trial balance ties out after every scenario. Full regression history: 30/30 suites green (29 prior + this phase's new suite), the new suite re-run 3x standalone to confirm the concurrency scenarios are deterministic, not lucky timing. tsc/eslint/vitest(1328)/build/12 governance audits all clean -- no new error codes, RBAC ops, or schema migrations needed. Honest boundaries carried forward: invoice cancellation does not reverse consumption rows (a pre-existing gap predating this phase, not introduced by it -- voiding any partially-paid invoice, by any payment method, does not currently reverse the payment side) and Treasury payment reversal remains explicitly not_implemented, both documented rather than silently expanded into scope.
